extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and experienced screenwriters (feature, short, TV, animation, and game narrative writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Catalog page listing Sundance Collab courses and events that teach screenwriting craft, story development, drafting, revision, pitching, and narrative design across feature, short, TV, animation, and games formats. Includes course-level targets (e.g., page counts), feedback/evaluation guidance, and workshop/review formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core elements of a feature screenplay / develop idea into outline
rubrics_metrics.description: "Learn the core elements of writing a screenplay for a feature film" and "develop a new script idea into an outline that can be used to write your first draft."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-paced course for Beginner to Intermediate writers; emphasis on learning and applying core elements so an idea becomes an actionable outline that supports drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short film screenplay development and page-length target
rubrics_metrics.description: "Designated homework assignments are reviewed by a Sundance Advisor and designed to move you closer to your completed short screenplay (5-15 pages)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eight-week self-paced course; measurable completion target (5–15 pages); iterative homework with advisor review to develop voice, storytelling skill, and a finished short script.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature screenplay first-draft length and completion target
rubrics_metrics.description: "Move from outline to completing a first draft of your screenplay (90-120 pages)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intermediate-level course designed to carry writers from outline through a full first draft; explicit page-count expectation for feature-length scripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revising and preparing your script to pitch (polish + pitch readiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Revise your feature film screenplay with an accomplished screenwriter as your guide... comprehensive approach to refining your script and preparing to pitch it to industry professionals."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Live online, multi-week course (advanced level) focused on substantive revision and packaging the script for pitching to agents, executives, financiers, talent, and other industry gatekeepers.

rubrics_metrics.name: How industry insiders evaluate writing / defending core story elements
rubrics_metrics.description: "Learn how industry insiders evaluate your writing, which core story elements you must defend, and how to discern which feedback will actually elevate your script to its best version."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshop-style guidance on reading and responding to notes; practice 'looking past the surface to find "the note behind the note."' Teaches prioritization of notes and defending essential story choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative design for games: directing player journey and maintaining engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: "Learn how narrative design serves as the framework in video games, directing the player's journey and maintaining sustained engagement."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisor Studio session focused on how to structure interactive narrative, design player-directed story beats, and sustain engagement across gameplay rather than linear screen time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding and shaping your voice, visual style, characters, and emotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections and master classes emphasize "finding your voice and visual style," "finding & shaping your screenplay's story," and work on "building characters, emotion and story."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curated talks and master classes from experienced filmmakers focusing on personal voice, visual storytelling, character development, and emotional stakes as central evaluative and creative criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making a script that gets past gatekeepers / grabs reader attention
rubrics_metrics.description: "Start writing that script that gets past gatekeepers and grabs your reader’s attention — whether it's an assistant, an agent, an executive, a financier, or the talent you want on screen."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical emphasis on clarity, hook, and commercial/readability considerations so a script can succeed in early-reader contexts and industry submission pipelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animation writing: crafting emotionally resonant scripts and process
rubrics_metrics.description: "Craft emotionally resonant scripts with Julia Cho (Turning Red)... animation is a powerful and dynamic language for storytelling."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on animation-specific storytelling techniques, emotional resonance, and creative processes unique to animated formats as distinct criteria from live-action scripting.
